When admins try to delete a single authentication method (AuthInfo) entry for a user, the request fails with a "Method Not Supported" error instead of actually removing it. This happens whenever the underlying storage mode is still routing through the older legacy storage path (the modes that haven't fully switched over to the new unified storage yet); those configurations were never given the ability to process single-item deletes and simply reject the request outright. Newer storage configurations that bypass legacy storage entirely already support deleting a single entry correctly, so the problem only affects the legacy-routed setups. We need users to be able to remove one specific auth method for one specific user (identified by the user and the auth method/module in question) without deleting anything else, and the delete request should succeed and actually remove that row instead of returning an error. The desired behavior is that all storage modes behave consistently: attempting to delete a single AuthInfo entry should work end-to-end regardless of which storage path is currently active, giving users a reliable way to remove an auth method association.
tasks.goldTitle: IAM: Implement AuthInfo delete for legacy storage

criteria.behavior: Requesting deletion of one AuthInfo entry (identified by the user plus the auth method/module) while the storage mode routes through the legacy path now succeeds rather than failing with a "method not supported" error, and the underlying auth-method row for that user and module is actually removed from storage.
A single-entry delete removes only the targeted user/module association: other auth methods belonging to the same user, and auth-method entries belonging to other users, are left in place.
After a successful single-entry delete, a subsequent read of that same entry reports not-found.

A successful single-entry delete responds with the representation of the entry that was removed (matching the requested entry identity) and signals that the removal was immediate rather than deferred/graceful.

Attempting to delete an entry that does not exist yields a not-found error rather than a success or an unrelated error — covering both the case where the referenced user does not exist and the case where the user exists but has no association for the requested auth method (including a repeat delete of an already-deleted entry).
When a delete-validation callback is supplied and rejects the operation, that rejection is returned to the caller and no auth-method row is removed.
Deleting a whole collection of AuthInfo entries continues to be rejected as an unsupported operation, so enabling single-entry deletes does not broaden into bulk deletes.

On the newer unified storage path, a single-entry delete request for a user that cannot be found, or for an entry that is already absent, completes without error (treated as a no-op) instead of surfacing a failure.

The code editor supports several languages for syntax highlighting, but the list of supported languages and their display labels is duplicated in multiple places across the product (for example, the shared code editor's own options and the notebook feature's language picker). Whenever a new language is added to the code editor, someone has to remember to manually update the notebook's language picker and labels too, otherwise the notebook won't offer the new language even though the editor itself supports it. This is error-prone and creates ongoing maintenance work.

We want a single, shared source of truth for supported languages (with their labels and highlighting behavior) that all features using the code editor can read from, so the notebook's language picker automatically shows any newly supported language without needing separate changes.

Additionally, we want to add support for editing INI/properties-style configuration files in the code editor. Since this is a less common use case, the parsing logic for it should not be loaded up front for every user of the editor — it should only be fetched and loaded when someone actually selects or needs INI syntax highlighting, consistent with how other less-common languages are already loaded on demand.

Note that INI highlighting may use a different syntax-highlighting engine than some of the editor's other languages, so token colors for INI may look slightly different from other languages in the editor — that's an acceptable tradeoff for now. This change only affects the shared editor component's language list and the notebook's language picker; it does not affect the separate provisioning viewer, which is being handled independently.
tasks.goldTitle: CodeMirror: Add shared language registry and lazy INI support

criteria.behavior: A single shared registry maps each supported editor language ID to its human-readable display label, and it is exported from the shared UI package's public surface so other features can read language metadata without redefining it.

The type/set of languages accepted by the code editor is derived from that shared registry, so adding an entry to the registry is sufficient to make the language accepted by the editor with no second list to update.

The notebook's language picker builds its highlighted-language options and their display labels from the shared registry rather than from a local duplicate list, so a language newly added to the registry appears in the picker (with its shared label) without further changes to the notebook code.

INI/properties-style configuration is a supported editor language: selecting it is accepted by the editor and produces a working syntax-highlighting configuration (a language is actually active in the editor state), and it appears in the notebook picker labelled "INI".

The INI parsing/highlighting code is not imported eagerly by the editor module graph; it is fetched only when INI highlighting is actually requested, matching the on-demand loading used for the editor's other languages.
Reading the shared language registry does not pull in any language parser or highlighting code, so consumers such as the picker get labels and IDs without loading editor language implementations.
Repeated requests for INI highlighting reuse the previously loaded highlighting configuration instead of re-fetching or rebuilding it.

Languages the editor cannot highlight continue to behave as before: plain text and the deliberately unhighlighted offered languages still appear in the picker with their own labels, and an arbitrary stored language value is preserved and rendered unhighlighted rather than coerced or dropped.

In the notebook editor, when you click into a cell and then hover over a different cell, both cells show their controls (drag handle, add button, actions bar) at the same time instead of only the one being interacted with. This makes it look like two cells are offering the same menu simultaneously, which is confusing. The controls should only appear for the cell the pointer is currently over, except that if a control (like the drag handle) has keyboard focus, it should stay visible even when the pointer moves away.

Separately, when collapsing a query row on a panel cell that has a long query, the datasource icon gets clipped and shows as only a sliver, and the query name disappears entirely. Since the query text already supports being cut off with an ellipsis, it should be the one to shrink and give up space first, so the query name and datasource picker always stay fully visible and readable. We currently have no visibility into how many dashboards use the newer text panel capabilities (mermaid diagrams, handlebars templating, data macros, per-row rendering), which makes it hard to justify further investment in these features. When a dashboard loads, if it contains at least one text panel and the instance has the newer text panel features enabled, we need a single usage event recorded for that dashboard load. The event should report, aggregated across all text panels on the dashboard: how many panels' content contains a mermaid diagram (either as a code fence or as an HTML element classed "mermaid"), how many contain a handlebars-style `{{ }}` expression, how many contain a data-linking macro like `${__value}`, `${__field}`, `${__data}`, or `${__series}`, and how many are configured with the "per row" rendering mode. The event must also include the dashboard's identifier so this usage data can later be joined against existing dashboard-load tracking to measure adoption relative to total dashboard views. This should fire exactly once per dashboard load regardless of how many text panels are present, not once per panel.
tasks.goldTitle: Text: Track feature usage on dashboard load

criteria.behavior: When a dashboard finishes loading and it contains at least one text panel (with the newer text panel capabilities enabled on the instance), exactly one usage event is recorded for that dashboard load — a single aggregated event regardless of whether the dashboard has one or many text panels, not one event per panel.

The recorded event reports four counts aggregated over all text panels on the dashboard: the number of panels whose content contains a mermaid diagram, the number containing a handlebars-style `{{ ... }}` expression, the number containing a data-linking macro, and the number configured with the per-row rendering mode. Each count increments at most once per panel even if a feature appears multiple times in that panel's content.
The recorded event includes the dashboard's unique identifier so the usage data can be joined against existing dashboard-load tracking.
Mermaid content is detected both when written as a fenced code block labelled mermaid and when written as an HTML element carrying the class "mermaid".
No usage event is recorded when the loaded dashboard contains no text panels.
No usage event is recorded when the newer text panel capabilities are not enabled, including when only one of the two required feature toggles is on and when neither is on.
The data-macro count recognises each of the `${__value}`, `${__field}`, `${__data}` and `${__series}` macros, including when they are used with a suffix such as `${__value.text}`.
